title: Finite homogeneous initial forms give one-step ideal approximation
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $J,K\subseteq A$ ideals, and suppose $\operatorname{gr}_J(A)$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring] is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. There exist $t\geq 0$, degrees $d_i\geq 0$ and elements $h_i\in K\cap J^{d_i}$ for $i\in\{1,\ldots,t\}$ such that for every $n\geq 0$ and $x\in K\cap J^n$, there are $a_i\in J^{\max(0,n-d_i)}$ with $x-\sum_i a_i h_i\in K\cap J^{n+1}$. No completeness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, lines 23022–23063), steps 3–4 (homogeneous initial ideal generators and one-step approximation)

proof.text: Define the initial form of x in J^n as the degree-n direct-sum inclusion of its quotient class. Form the ideal spanned by the range of all such initial forms of x in K intersect J^n. Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing and Submodule.fg_span_iff_fg_span_finset_subset extract a finite subset of this same range. Choose preimages of these finitely many forms and reindex them by Fin t using Fintype.equivFin; their degrees and representatives give d and h in K intersect J^(d i). Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun expresses every initial form as a finite sum of products with these selected forms. This does not require constructing a homogeneous ideal or homogenizing arbitrary generators.

For any associated-graded coefficient q and a degree-d initial form of h, prove by DirectSum.induction_on that its degree-n product component is represented by a*h with a in J^(n-d). Zero uses a=0; addition adds the two coefficients. On a homogeneous degree-k summand, Submodule.Quotient.induction_on gives a representative in J^k. Ideal.associatedGraded_mul computes the product in degree k+d. If k+d=n, Ideal.mul_mem_mul and pow_add put a*h in J^n and Nat.add_sub_cancel identifies the coefficient ideal. Otherwise DirectSum.of_eq_of_ne makes the component zero and a=0 suffices.

Apply DirectSum.component at degree n to the finite-sum equality for the initial form of x. Replace each product component by its representative a_i*h_i from the previous step. The quotient map preserves finite sums. Submodule.Quotient.eq identifies the equality of quotient classes with x minus the sum lying in J^(n+1). Ideal closure under multiplication, sums and subtraction gives membership in K. Empty families, degree-zero generators and n below a generator degree are covered by the same proof; no completeness or Noetherianity of A is used.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_associatedGraded_ideal_approximation {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    (J K : Ideal A) [IsNoetherianRing (associatedGraded J)] :
    ∃ (t : ℕ) (d : Fin t → ℕ) (h : Fin t → A),
      (∀ i, h i ∈ K) ∧ (∀ i, h i ∈ J ^ (d i)) ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : A), x ∈ K → x ∈ J ^ n →
        ∃ a : Fin t → A, (∀ i, a i ∈ J ^ (n - d i)) ∧
          x - ∑ i, a i * h i ∈ K ∧ x - ∑ i, a i * h i ∈ J ^ (n + 1)
